correctness.rationale: All four two-agent and all 216 three-agent strict profiles are exhaustively checked. Two serial-dictatorship implementations agree; direct lexicographic signature maximization and an exact base-4 weighted formulation return identical rank-maximal sets. The 54-profile failure set is independently summarized by rank-maximal-set size, signature transitions, and nine object-relabeling classes.

evidence: Abdulkadiroğlu-Sönmez establish serial-dictatorship-based house allocation as a canonical mechanism.
Irving et al. define the matching signature and rank-maximality and give algorithms for computing rank-maximal matchings.
The rank-maximal paper explicitly allows multiple rank-maximal matchings and studies the objective independently of serial-dictatorship priorities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources cover the two ingredients separately but do not imply when a fixed-priority serial-dictatorship outcome is rank-maximal. That comparison requires an additional profile-level argument or exhaustive classification.

value.rationale: Serial dictatorship and rank-maximal matching encode two central but different allocation principles: fixed-priority incentive compatibility and lexicographic rank satisfaction. The first market size where these principles conflict, together with its exact prevalence and symmetry classes, is a natural structural boundary with direct mechanism-design interpretation.
